summary: Most material numbers check out against primary sources: HSC §1569.185 fee table; DHCS ALW Tier 1–5 rates ($95.69–$270.80), G9002/G9001/T2017/T2024; the 2023 ALW comparison; ALW enrollment/waitlist (14,831 / 15,910, March 2026); SSI/SSP $1,626.07 and $1,444.07/$182; the $16.90 2026 minimum wage; every BLS OEWS May 2025 CA wage used (17.51, 40.01, 39.59, 23.03, 22.08 — pulled from BLS OESServices); CareScout $7,000/$6,200; APFM $5,739/$6,850; Genworth $70,800; NIC 88.4%; USDA food $329.90/$363.90; EDD 2026 rates; LLC-1/LLC-12; the $800 FTB tax; admin cert fees ($100/$140/$300; 80/60 hrs; 40 CE incl. 8 dementia; 60-day exam); orientation $54.85; the 90–120 day timeline, CAB address/phone/email; ASCP, ACB, ombudsman and CDSS phones; 22 CCR §§87155(a)(13), 87307, 87303, 87405, 87411, 87415, 87465, 87507, 87632, 87706; HSC §§1569.605, 1569.616, 1569.625, 1569.69, 1569.84, 1569.85; W&I §15630; PPIC; the CHHS RCFE counts (recomputed exactly); San Diego FMR. Staffing meets the cited rules (one person on premises 24/7 beats the §87415 on-call rule for <16 beds). P&L recomputation matches the narrative table. Main problems: (1) the $17.51 caregiver wage is below 2026 local minimums in LA, San Diego, San Jose and SF, and at those minimums the 6-bed default turns unprofitable; (2) the mandatory FTB LLC fee ($900/$2,500/$6,000) is missing from every configuration; (3) the Medi-Cal enrollment fee is $750 for 2026, not $730; (4) the initial/application fee is described as charged at license issuance when it is paid with the application; (5) checklist[5] tells operators to get a city business license, which HSC §1569.185(b)(2) bars for 6-or-fewer homes. Not independently retrievable (HUD blocked): non-San Diego FMR values; WCIRB 9070 class rate (already in not_claimed).

issues.correct: 17.51 statewide is valid, but add a local-minimum sensitivity: City of Los Angeles $18.42 (7/1/2026), unincorporated LA County $18.47, San Diego city $17.75, San Jose $18.45, Santa Clara $18.70, San Francisco $19.61
issues.evidence: BLS OEWS May 2025 CA 31-1120 mean $17.51 (median $16.50) confirmed via BLS OESServices CA table, and it is above the $16.90 state minimum. But $17.51 is below the legal minimum in the high-cost metros the report uses as rent examples (LA, San Diego, San Jose, SF). Recomputed with the bundle's own formulas at 88% occupancy: at $18.42 for caregivers, rcfe6_private goes from +$781/mo to -$134/mo, rcfe6x2_private from +$2,081 to +$514, and rcfe6_mixed_alw from -$1,142 to -$2,057. So the 'profitable' 6-bed default turns negative in LA.
issues.fix: Keep 17.51 with S38. Add a source for 2026 local minimum wages (DWT July-2026 list and CalChamber Jan-2026 list, https://hrcalifornia.calchamber.com/articles/california-local-minimum-wage-rates-increases-starting-january-1-2026). In financial_narrative and risks, say the 6-bed private model goes break-even or negative at the LA/San Diego/Bay Area local minimum, and tell users to set wage_hourly to max(17.51, local minimum).

issues.evidence: FTB LLC fee schedule: $250,000–$499,999 = $900; $500,000–$999,999 = $2,500; $1,000,000–$4,999,999 = $6,000. Annual revenue at default occupancy from the bundle's own inputs: rcfe6_private $32,521×12 = $390k; rcfe6x2 $65,042×12 = $780k; rcfe15 $83,523×12 = $1,002k. No configuration includes the fee, and the note's '$900–$2,500 for these sizes' is wrong for the 15-bed model, which falls in the $6,000 bracket.
issues.fix: Add a fixed opex line 'California LLC fee (gross-receipts based) ÷ 12', source S55: 75 base; opex_overrides 208.33 for rcfe6x2_private and 500 for rcfe15_private. Change the note to '$900 / $2,500 / $6,000 depending on total CA income'. In checklist[2], add the $6,000 bracket for $1M–$4,999,999 and say a 15-bed home at the model's prices crosses $1M.

issues.current: Get a city business license (RCFEs serving 6 or fewer are exempt from business taxes and fees other family dwellings don't pay). ... cite: HSC §1569.84
issues.correct: For 6 or fewer: a local jurisdiction may not impose a business license, fee or tax for operating the facility (HSC §1569.185(b)(2)). Check local minimum wage. For 7+ beds, check city business license rules.
issues.evidence: HSC §1569.185(b)(2): 'A local jurisdiction shall not impose a business license, fee, or tax for the privilege of operating a facility licensed under this chapter that serves six or fewer persons.' §1569.84 is about fire-inspection fees, not business licenses.
issues.fix: Rewrite the instructions as above. Change cite to 'HSC §1569.185(b)(2); DIR MW-2026' and source_id to S1.

The 2026 total grant of $1,626.07 is official (S5).
